title: Conjecture 2 (Bensmail et al. [3])
statement_text: There is a function $f$ such that, for any fixed tree $T$ with maximum degree $\Delta_T$, every $f(\Delta_T)$-edge-connected graph with minimum degree at least $f(|E(T)|)$ and number of edges divisible by $|E(T)|$ has a $T$-decomposition.
context_text: This is a strengthened version of the Barát–Thomassen conjecture posed in [3], where the path case (T a path) was also proved with 24-edge-connectivity. The conjecture as stated for general trees was subsequently disproved by the current paper's authors (in [7]) even for trees of maximum degree three.
paper_contribution: Proves the path case with optimal 3-edge-connectivity (replacing the 24-edge-connectivity of [3]), establishing that $f(2) = 3$ is achievable; notes the general conjecture is false for trees of maximum degree three.
notes: The conjecture carries no widely-used name; it is numbered Conjecture 2 within this paper. The bibliography entry [3] is not spelled out in the extracted text, so full attribution details are unavailable.

title: Conjecture 5
statement_text: There is a function $f$ such that, for any fixed tree $T$ with $m$ leaves, every $f(m)$-edge-connected graph with minimum degree at least $f(|E(T)|)$ and number of edges divisible by $|E(T)|$ has a $T$-decomposition.
context_text: For graphs $G$ and $H$, an $H$-decomposition of $G$ is a partition of $E(G)$ into sets each of which forms an isomorphic copy of $H$; this requires $|E(H)|$ to divide $|E(G)|$. The Barát–Thomassen conjecture, proved by Bensmail, Harutyunyan, Le, Merker and Thomassé, states that for every tree $T$ there is $k_T$ such that every $k_T$-edge-connected graph with number of edges divisible by $|E(T)|$ has a $T$-decomposition; its case where $T$ is the claw $K_{1,3}$ is equivalent to the weak $3$-flow conjecture (every sufficiently edge-connected graph has a nowhere-zero $3$-flow), proved by Thomassen and improved by Lovász, Thomassen, Wu and Zhang. A strengthening posed earlier asked for a function $f$ such that every $f(\Delta_T)$-edge-connected graph with minimum degree at least $f(|E(T)|)$ and number of edges divisible by $|E(T)|$ has a $T$-decomposition, where $\Delta_T$ is the maximum degree of $T$; it holds for paths but the authors showed it fails already for some trees of maximum degree three. The present conjecture is the authors' alternative, bounding the edge-connectivity in terms of the number of leaves of $T$ instead. The paper's main result is that for every $\ell$ there is $d(\ell)$ such that every $3$-edge-connected graph with minimum degree at least $d(\ell)$ and number of edges divisible by $\ell$ decomposes into paths of length $\ell$ (edges), which is optimal in the connectivity and shows one can take $f(2)=3$; the existence of $f(3)$ would already contain the claw case. The authors would find it very interesting to have a proof not using the claw case as a starting point.
